To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the IoT is a socio-technical space that craftspeople can inhabit and shape.
craftspeople’s workspaces are socio-technical arrangements where people and technology interact in complex and dynamic ways.

(a) craftspeople use a wide range of tools, many of which are not designed for craft, (b) craftspeople are aware of the limitations of these tools, (c) craftspeople are willing to adapt to the tools that are available, (d) the tools are not necessarily designed to be flexible or adaptable, (e) the craftspeople have to work with the tools as they are, (f) the craftspeople are willing and able to adapt their practices to the tools
In summary, our research is concerned with

how people, tools and technologies interact with one another in the context of productivity, and how the IoT can be understood as a socio-technical phenomenon that is both flexible and respectful of individual agency.
how people and tools are connected in the context of the Internet of Things, and how these relationships are experienced and understood in terms of productivity and craft.
the ways in which people and technologies are interwoven in the everyday, and how these relationships might change as we move towards a more connected society.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study has demonstrated how the IoT can be understood as a socio-technical space that is not only about technology, but also about human relationships and the materiality of the everyday.
the IoT should be designed in such a way as to be companionable to the human and non-human actors that comprise the social and material fabric of everyday life.
the Internet of Things is not a panacea for productivity, nor is it a threat to the human condition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are interested in the ways in which craft and IoT are similar in their approach to the material world and the ways in which they are different in their approach to human agency.
we have developed a theoretical model that explains the socio-technical space of the Internet of Things.
the IoT is not a new phenomenon, and that the Internet of Things is already happening.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can understand the IoT as a set of socio-technical practices and arrangements, which we can use to develop policy and interventions to support the IoT as a socio-technical space.
the socio-technical fabric of everyday life is a complex, multi-layered and dynamic system.
the Internet of Things is not a new technology.
